prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create the first production sprite atlas for Elements - Icons. The two supplied pictures are STYLE REFERENCES, not subjects to copy.
Rustic, earnest old-fashioned COLOURED WOODCUT. Match the supplied references' warm black, dull ochre, clay/rust red, slate blue, muted olive and creamy carved cuts, but visibly simpler and less polished than the first reference: a small number of broad confident cuts, occasional knife slips, uneven angular contours, slightly crooked handmade things, thin missed patches in ink and colour plates shifted slightly beyond or short of their black outlines. Imperfect registration must look printed, not blurred. No smooth gradients, modeled digital shading, tiny decorative hatching, glossy highlights, outline stickers, cute toy proportions, circular badges, frames or presentation shadows. Humble functional objects, easily recognised at 56 pixels. Natural, clear silhouettes before texture. Transparent outside each object.
EXACTLY 20 distinct icons in FIVE equal columns and FOUR equal rows. A wide 5:4 atlas, ideally 2000x1600. Every object fits inside its own equal rectangular cell with 15% transparent margin on every side. Strict grid alignment makes mechanical extraction possible. No labels, numbers, text or drawn grid. Do not connect neighbouring cells. All twenty have consistent visual weight.
READING ORDER, left to right, top to bottom:
1. Earth: loose dark fine soil, low mound, small irregular crumbs, not a boulder or planet
2. Water: three broad slate-blue water ripples and one clear falling droplet, no vessel
3. Air: three long broken pale slate-blue wind strokes carrying one small leaf, no cloud
4. Fire: a modest campfire, three irregular rust-red flames above two black logs
5. Stone: one large angular grey fieldstone, no pile
6. Clay: a squat lump of damp red-brown clay with a thumb indentation
7. Brick: one blunt rectangular fired clay-red building brick
8. Sand: a low small ochre sand heap with a few loose grains, distinctly lighter and finer than earth
9. Glass: one pale slate-blue transparent rectangular glass pane with one broken irregular edge, not a window frame
10. Wood: three short rough barked branches/logs bundled loosely
11. Planks: three rough sawn tan timber boards with broad simple grain cuts
12. Plant: one ordinary leafy green plant with roots and soil, no flower
13. Grain: three ripe ochre wheat ears and a small pile of threshed grain
14. Fruit: three recognisable apples, red and ochre, one leaf
15. Plant fiber: a loose hank of long pale straw-coloured plant fibres, no wooden spool
16. Thread: ochre thread wound on a plain small wooden spool, one loose trailing strand
17. Cloth: an undyed cream folded cloth with irregular frayed edge
18. Rope: a coarse brown rope in an open coil with clearly twisted strands
19. Rain: a small irregular slate-blue cloud and six long slanting raindrops
20. Flowers: three modest red field flowers on stems in a loose bunch, not a planted shrub
Make this more rustic than the polished reference atlas: fewer cuts, more awkwardness, uneven inking and imperfect colour registration, while keeping each object structurally clear.
